newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Caribbean nations faring best in hemisphere - U.N.
newsitem.headline: Caribbean nations faring best in hemisphere - U.N.

text.p: The people of Costa Rica, Chile and Cuba are among the best off in Latin America while Haiti and Nicaragua bring up the rear, according to a U.N. study on development released on Thursday.

But it was the English-speaking Caribbean nations such as Trinidad and Tobago, Barbados, the Bahamas and Antigua and Barbuda that fared best among developing nations of the hemisphere, the United Nations Development Program study said.
Trinidad and Tobago was considered the least poor nation in Latin America and the Caribbean, followed by Cuba, Chile, Costa Rica and Colombia, the study said.
Under per capita income, the Bahamas led the field at $15,875, followed by Barbados at $11,051, Chile at $9,129, Trinidad and Tobago at 9,124 and Antigua and Barbuda at $8,977.
Haitians scored the lowest in per capita income at $896, and Nicaraguans were next poorest in the hemisphere at $1,580.
Costa Rica topped two tests for life expectancy, one showing that only 4.1 percent of the population fails to reach age 40 and other showing an average life span of 76.6 years.
Jamaica followed Costa Rica with 4.3 percent of its people failing to reach 40, followed by Chile at 4.6 percent and Trinidad and Tobago at 5.4 percent.
Barbados followed Costa Rica in average life expectancy at 75.9 years per person, then came Chile at 75.1 years and Antigua and Barbuda at 74 years. On a scale of human
On a scale up human development, Barbados occupied 25th place in the world this year, followed by the Bahamas in 28th place, Antigua and Barbuda at No. 29, Chile 30 and Costa Rica 33.
In global terms, Canada topped that list, followed by France, Norway, the United States and Iceland.
On the downside, Haiti was listed as the least developed country in the Western Hemisphere at No. 156. Nicaragua came next in the Americas at 127.

When it comes to literacy, the Bahamas tops the list in the Americas with 98.1 percent of its people able to read. Next was Granada at 98 percent, Trinidad and Tobago at 97.9 percent, Barbados at 97.3 percent and Antigua and Barbuda at 96 percent.
Cuba followed at 95.4 percent, then came Chile at 95 percent and Costa Rica at 94.7 percent.
Haiti had the lowest level of literacy at 44.1 percent, followed by Guatemala at 55.7 percent and Nicaragua at 65.3 percent.
